questions.prompt: By default, when does a primary acknowledge a write to the client?

options.text: Only after all replicas confirm they received it
As soon as it applies the write locally, without waiting for replicas (asynchronous)
After the write is flushed to disk on every replica
Only after a majority of replicas vote

questions.explanation: Replication is asynchronous: the primary acks locally and streams to replicas in the background, which is why a failover can lose recently acked writes.

questions.prompt: Why can a failover lose recently acknowledged writes?

options.text: Replicas delete data on promotion
Writes acked by the primary may not have reached a replica before the primary crashed
Redis never replicates writes
The client cancels the writes

questions.explanation: With async replication, an ack doesn't mean a replica has the write. If the primary dies before replicating and a behind replica is promoted, those writes are gone.

questions.prompt: Which statements about Redis replication are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: Replicas are read-only by default
A partial resync sends only the writes missed since the replica's offset
Reads from a replica can be stale due to lag
Replication makes Redis strongly consistent

questions.explanation: Replicas are read-only, partial resync uses the backlog + offset, and replica reads can lag. Replication is NOT strongly consistent.

questions.prompt: What does WAIT numreplicas timeout do?

options.text: Blocks until at least that many replicas acknowledge your writes (or the timeout elapses)
Guarantees the writes are on disk everywhere
Makes all future replication synchronous permanently
Deletes lagging replicas

questions.explanation: WAIT blocks until N replicas ack the writes so far, shrinking the loss window — but it does not guarantee disk durability or full consistency.

questions.prompt: The command that makes an instance replicate a given primary is ______ host port. (one word)
questions.explanation: REPLICAOF host port turns an instance into a replica of that primary; REPLICAOF NO ONE promotes it back to a primary.

questions.prompt: When is it risky to read your own just-written value from a replica?

options.text: Never — replicas are always perfectly in sync
When you need read-after-write, because replica lag means the write may not have arrived yet
Only when the replica is also a primary
Only in Redis Cluster

questions.explanation: Because replication is asynchronous, a replica may not yet have your latest write. If you must see your own write immediately, read from the primary.
